caption:
As I break my 7 day fast with 2819 church I am proud to say that I have come really far, but I still have a long way to go. Over the past few months my faith has been tested over and over and to tell the truth I have been sinking. I lost touch with Christ. And I could feel it. I have been following 2819 church since this time last year and Pastor Mitchell has saved me countless times getting me closer to God and I couldn’t be more grateful. 

Giving up food, social media, and many other things this week has shown me a lot. The biggest reward I got from it was getting closer to God. No matter what happens in my life I will prevail because he will forever be on my side. And I will forever have faith in him. 

I usually don’t post stuff like this but I believe God put me on this earth to serve, lead, and inspire. By not sharing I feel as though I would be disobeying him. I pray that whoever is struggling with their faith uses this post, these words, to get over the hump. And fully give their life to our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ. 

I finally feel free. This is only the beginning. THANK YOU GOD!

“Trust in the Lord with all your heart, and do not lean on your own understanding.”
‭‭Proverbs‬ ‭3‬:‭5‬ ‭ESV‬‬

Thank you Texas Tech and thank you Football❤️

caption:
It was a long time ago when I realized I was the one that had to do something that’s never been done. 

To be the first one in my family to graduate means the world to me. Setting the standard for the generations that come after me in my family was one of the most important things I could do. Not only my family but young kids who grew up like I did in Milwaukee. It ain’t easy. Leaving an impact is something I will continue to do. 

I knew I had to be the example for my young ones and it’s been a tough task but I’m never one to give up. 

Whatever happens next in this divine journey will be nothing but greatness. I have the best family, friends, team, and support system to help me get through it. But more importantly I have the utmost faith in God!

LOCO IS FAR FROM FINISHED! 

LLP🕊️❤️

Happy One Year Anniversary❤️

We’ve spent almost a decade doing life in our own way — on & off, growing up, finding our way back to each other — and now one full year of calling you my wife feels unreal in the best way. After 9 years of history and 3 years of being inseparable, today isn’t just about one year of marriage… it’s about how far we’ve come together.

We’ve seen each other at our best and our worst. We’ve learned, forgiven, laughed, cried, and chose each other again and again. And somehow, after everything, I love you more than I ever have.

You’re not just my wife, you’re my best friend, my peace, my home. Thank you for standing beside me, growing with me, and believing in us even when the road wasn’t easy.

Here’s to our past that shaped us, our present that grounds us, and our future that excites me more than anything. I’d choose you in every lifetime.

I love you — always and forever 🤍

caption:
BREAKING NEWS: 🚨 NiJaree Canady has officially been named to Forbes 30 Under 30, becoming the only softball athlete selected to the list this year.

After two standout seasons at Stanford, Canady transferred to Texas Tech and delivered one of the most dominant seasons we’ve seen in modern college softball: 240 innings pitched, 319 strikeouts, and a 1.11 ERA, leading the Red Raiders to the WCWS finals and earning the Honda Sport Award as the nation’s top softball player.

Off the field, she signed back-to-back seven-figure NIL deals: a $1,050,000 contract followed by a $1.2 million renewal, the largest known NIL agreements in college softball history.

Her impact spans performance, visibility, and athlete value. This Forbes recognition marks another moment in a career that’s already making history.

For more softball media, culture, & community, follow @welivesoftball_ 🫶🥎

-

Sources:
• Forbes — 30 Under 30 Sports List
• Sports Illustrated — Coverage of Canady’s NIL and 2025 season
• Yardbarker — 2025 stat line (240 IP, 319 K, 1.11 ERA)
• ESPN / KCBD — Reporting on NIL contract values

athlete.name: Skyler Gill-Howard
athlete.bio: A relentless force on the field, this defensive lineman combines relentless tenacity with strategic finesse. Hailing from a small town, he brings grit and heart, always striving for greatness.

caption:
Injury Statement:
“I won’t sit here and pretend this hasn’t been tough — because it has.

Getting injured on Homecoming night was devastating. As I lay on that field, feeling a pain I’ve never felt before, everything around me went quiet. I cried. Not just from the pain, but from the moment — knowing how badly I wanted to perform in front of my people. My mom, my grandma, my family… and it was taken away just like that.

But even in that moment, I stayed optimistic. When I threw up the Guns Up, the crowd lifted me. That energy saved me from going to a dark place. I couldn’t return to the game, but I put on a boot, stayed with my team, and we came out victorious. That’s what mattered.

Then the MRI came. It hit even harder — it was my birthday. I won’t lie, I shed some tears. But I also made a choice: to see it as a gift. A new challenge. A test of my mindset. I’ve never been injured in my life, and now I’m forced to slow down. But that doesn’t mean I stop.

This is what Staying the Course looks like. This is what Act As If Everything Works Out really means. I believe this injury is part of a bigger plan — a reminder that the work doesn’t stop, the dream doesn’t change, and most importantly showing God’s greatness.

We’re far from finished.
We’ve been counted out before — We’re not folding now.
This is just the beginning of the comeback.
ALL GLORY BE TO GOD”

- Skyler Gill Howard

The Hero’s Journey 

A LOCO PRESENTATION

caption:
chicken crust protein pizza…
decided to give this a try… and it’s solid. 

Base: 
-1 lb ground chicken 
-2 eggs 
-1/2 cup parmesan cheese 
-2 tsp garlic salt 
-1 tsp italian seasoning 
-1/2 tsp black pepper 

Toppings: 
-1/2 cup pizza sauce 
-1 cup mozzarella cheese 
-20 slices of turkey pepperoni 

Cooking: 
1.Preheat oven to 400°, line a baking tray
with parchment paper or foil (foil was all i had)
2.Mix chicken, eggs, parmesan, garlic powder, Italian
seasoning, salt and pepper in a bowl.
3.Spread mixture thin on tray into a circle or
rectangle.
4.Bake 25 mins until golden, let set 5 mins.
5. Turn oven up to 450°, add sauce, cheese
and toppings.
6.Bake another 10 mins until cheese is melty and bubbling.

Macros: 
1434 cals
197 protein🔥
20 carb
67 fat

caption:
Yesterday morning, my beautiful mom left this earth to go to her eternal home in Heaven. God couldn’t have chosen a better woman to be my mom. She was the strongest, most fun, and most competitive woman I’ve ever known. I admired her faith in God. I’m so thankful for all of the memories, laughs, time spent in the front yard throwing ball, all of our beach days, and so many other things I was blessed to share with her. 

Praise be to God, my mom is healed and in His presence! Jesus gives us the free gift of salvation if we accept Him: peaceful and everlasting life when our time in this world ends. I’m going to miss my favorite golf partner, but I’ll see you later, Mama! I love you forever! ❤️

caption:
Texas Tech long snapper Rylan Vagana made the trip to Eau Claire Wisconsin to chase perfection!

This was Rylan’s first time to Eau Claire and was recommended by former Texas Tech snapper Jackson Knotts. We started with our initial assessment where we noticed that he had a tough time controlling his follow through and body in general. 

A big part of his issue was from his grip being unbalanced. If you don’t start balanced, you can’t end balanced. He was also out of sequence and overly aggressive with his start. 

After we balanced his hands, we spent a lot of time focusing on his ability to accelerate his snap into a controlled follow through position. This made a huge difference! He not only snapped faster but also had more control!

I’m looking forward to continuing to help Rylan grow and chase perfection!

caption:
Dear Brock Softball,
I thanked God everyday that I got to wake up every Tuesday and Friday, knowing that I got to put on your jersey. 
4 years of my life dedicated to you, and putting everything I had into this program. I wouldn't have wanted to be anywhere else to say the least. 
I want to thank my family, for always supporting  and pushing me to be my best self. The support system that I have from y'all will forever be my favorite part of the game.  I want to thank the Brock coaching staff my senior year, to never making me feel anything other than great. Thank you for always propelling me to rise and go above and beyond. To my teammates, from the past and present, thank you for making my journey at Brock unforgettable and making me grow love for the game.
To the Brock community, I cannot even begin to thank each and every one of you for your unwavering support. From littles, to bigs, thank you for always making me feel welcome and supported. Even through the rough times, I will forever be grateful for all of you.
That being said, I still got more time to play. TYJ. 
I am ready for this next chapter of my life, and I now know that I will have forever fans. Wreck em'.
But for now, with one of my hardest goodbyes..
#10, Mia Richards, is officially out. 💙💛

caption: Today and yesterday have been very important days for many High School softball programs. With the end of the season coming so soon and playoffs just now starting; there are many things to think about. For everyone who has made it,  and even the school that didn't make it,  but put in countless hours of hard work and dedication. Congratulations for a long, hard season. With that being said,  sometimes we push aside ourselves and how we feel as players and even humans. Not many people talk about it,  but it matters. Mental health should always come first, and you should never have to fight your battles alone. For those who have made it this far,  I wish yall the best of luck. To the schools that continue to put work in to become great and strive for perfection; I wish yall the best of luck. Check in on someone today,  make someone feel appreciated, love everyone around you. MENTAL HEALTH MATTERS! #mentalhealthawareness #playforsomethingbigger

it breaks my heart to say that my left ACL graft has failed for a 3rd time. but like the last 2 times, i’m determined to come back even stronger, and not let this injury be the reason i stop playing the sport i love. although this surgery was more intense and required grafting a tendon from my good knee to replace the ACL in the other, i know i can & will get back on the court again. i’m kind of a pro at this by now 🙂

this time, i went to a world-renowned knee specialist to ensure i have the best chance at this being my last ACL surgery ever. i plan to redshirt this year, and still play my final 2 seasons as a Red Raider.. (even though i’ll literally be 35 when i’m done.)

they do say 3rd time’s the charm :’) thank you to everyone who has supported me through it all. 18 will be back soon❤️‍🩹
